verdicts.question: Is the building currently under construction?
verdicts.photo_observation: Scaffolding tower along the side wall (pp.9-10), construction debris/rubble, broken fence panels and loose soil in the side passage (pp.6,9,10), patchy unfinished plaster at the base and around openings (pp.6,8), cement bags inside rooms (pp.7,9), loose unterminated wiring hanging from the meter box (p.10).
verdicts.rationale: Multiple clear under-construction cues across pages 5-10 support 'Yes'.

verdicts.question: In an under-construction building, are existing conduit pipes available for AC, DC cables, and earthing?
verdicts.designer_notes: All the cables in connection with this system execution have to be laid separately, following the given cable routing.
verdicts.photo_observation: No conduit pipes or sleeves visible along the documented route; p.8 caption says cables are taken out by drilling holes in the wall; p.7 caption says customer will lay input/output cables to the inverter location; p.9 says AC earthing cable to exit through the wall behind the door.
verdicts.rationale: Routing plan relies on new wall penetrations rather than existing conduits, consistent with 'No'. Concealed conduits cannot be fully ruled out from photos.

verdicts.question: What is the height of the building and how many floors does it have?
verdicts.photo_observation: Front elevation (p.5): ground level with stilt/porch parking and entrance, first floor with glass-railed balcony, second floor with window under a cantilevered roof slab - three levels total. Side elevation (p.6) shows three rows of windows. No headroom structure visible.
verdicts.rationale: Three visible levels match G+2; ~10 m overall height is plausible for a three-storey villa.

verdicts.question: Is the site photo matching with the building description?
verdicts.photo_observation: Building Exterior photo (p.5) shows a G+2 villa with paved front court; side photos (pp.6,9,10) show the same plastered facade, scaffolding and unfinished surroundings.
verdicts.rationale: Photos are consistent with the described G+2 under-construction villa.

verdicts.question: Is there an overhead HT line passing within a 10-meter radius of the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Thin overhead wire(s) cross the top of the Building Exterior photo (p.5) at roughly roof level, running from the left edge across the building. Conductor type/voltage cannot be determined (could be LT service, street-light or telecom cable). No poles or insulator strings visible.
verdicts.rationale: An overhead line is visible close to the building; photo cannot confirm it is not HT. Verify on site / via street-view.

verdicts.question: Can the delivery van/truck reach the material unloading point?
verdicts.photo_observation: Wide paved forecourt directly in front of the building (p.5) with open approach from the road side; Material Delivery Route arrow drawn from the forecourt to the left side of the building.
verdicts.rationale: Open paved approach supports vehicle access to the front of the building; gate/road width beyond frame not visible.

verdicts.question: Are there any obstacles at the site that could hinder material lifting?
verdicts.photo_observation: Route to inverter room (p.6) runs through a narrow side passage with rubble, loose stones, leaning concrete fence panels, a timber prop and a hose on the ground; scaffolding stands in the side setback (pp.9,10). Materials are stored at ground level, and no rooftop/lifting route is documented.
verdicts.rationale: Debris and fence panels in the side passage could hinder material movement; not a clear contradiction since equipment is ground-floor only, but should be confirmed cleared before delivery.

verdicts.question: Where will the Inverter, DCDB, ACDB, Battery, etc. be located?
verdicts.designer_answer: All the equipment can be installed inside the room allocated for the inverter and batteries on the ground floor.
verdicts.photo_observation: 'Inverter room with cable routing' (p.7) shows an indoor tiled ground-floor room with INVERTER, Fuse box and BATTERY-3 Nos. marked on the plastered wall; p.6 shows ground-floor door into this room from the side passage.
verdicts.rationale: Photos and markup show a dedicated indoor ground-floor equipment room.

verdicts.question: Is a canopy required for protecting the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB?
verdicts.photo_observation: Equipment positions are marked inside an enclosed indoor room with roof slab and door (pp.7,9).
verdicts.rationale: Indoor location - no weather exposure, canopy not required.

verdicts.question: Did you discuss the location of the earth pits with the customer?
verdicts.designer_notes: The setback ground is available on the northwest side of the building (near the inverter room)
verdicts.photo_observation: p.9 shows the AC Earth Pit marked on bare soil in the side setback directly opposite the inverter-room door; 'Earth Pit Location' (p.10) shows the same long soil strip between the building and the boundary wall.
verdicts.rationale: Earth pit location is identified on photos next to the inverter room as described. The discussion itself and the NW compass direction cannot be verified visually.

verdicts.question: What's the inverter location decided with the client in case of String/SolarEdge/Hybrid?
verdicts.designer_answer: All the equipment can be installed inside the room allocated for the inverter and batteries on the ground floor.
verdicts.photo_observation: p.7 markup places INVERTER on the wall of the indoor ground-floor inverter/battery room, beside Fuse box and BATTERY-3 Nos.
verdicts.rationale: Inverter location clearly marked in the ground-floor room as stated.

verdicts.question: Where is the Internet Router located?
verdicts.designer_answer: Currently under construction. Internet router will be provided at the inverter location by the customer.
verdicts.photo_observation: No router, network point or LAN cabling visible in the inverter room (p.7) or elsewhere; building is visibly under construction.
verdicts.rationale: Absence of a router is consistent with the under-construction status stated by the designer.

verdicts.question: What's the Wi-Fi strength of the router near to the String inverter/Envoy?
verdicts.photo_observation: No router or Wi-Fi equipment visible in any photo; signal strength is not something photos can show.
verdicts.rationale: Consistent with under-construction status but not visually verifiable.

verdicts.question: Did you pin the site location in your WhatsApp when you were at the site?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not a photo-verifiable item. Page 1 contains a Google Maps link (13.030082, 77.742549) for the site.
verdicts.rationale: GMap coordinates exist in the report, but the WhatsApp pin cannot be verified from photos.

verdicts.question: What type of energy meter is currently installed?
verdicts.designer_notes: Building under construction. A 3-phase meter box is available, but no meter is fixed yet.
verdicts.photo_observation: Meter Box (p.10): left compartment has the meter position marked 'MAIN METER' but behind/below the label only loose unterminated red/yellow/blue/black conductors hang - no meter body. Three porcelain service cut-out fuses and a 4-way neutral link are fitted, indicating a 3-phase supply arrangement.
verdicts.rationale: No meter installed and 3-phase cut-outs/R-Y-B wiring present - matches designer note exactly.

verdicts.question: Is the Meter cubicle photo matching with the previous answer?
verdicts.photo_observation: Same p.10 photo: two-compartment steel meter box, empty meter position with loose phase wires, 3 cut-out fuses, unfinished DB wiring in right compartment.
verdicts.rationale: Meter cubicle photo matches '3-phase box, no meter fixed yet'.

verdicts.question: Has the termination point in the Main meter panel been identified?
verdicts.designer_notes: Building under construction. A 3-phase meter box is available, but no meter is fixed yet.
verdicts.photo_observation: Main meter panel (p.10) has no meter and only temporary/loose wiring. p.8 instead proposes a separate 'Input/Output MCB box' (4P 40A MCBs) beside the main meter for cable termination.
verdicts.rationale: No termination point inside the incomplete main panel is identifiable, consistent with 'No'; note p.8 does define a planned termination box adjacent to the meter.

verdicts.question: In Main meter panel, is empty space available for solar meter?
verdicts.photo_observation: Left compartment (p.10) is reserved for the main meter with cut-outs and neutral link; right compartment holds a DIN rail with a 4-pole MCB and dense loose wiring. No spare compartment visible. p.8 shows a separate box planned next to the main meter.
verdicts.rationale: Both compartments are allocated; no obvious free space for a solar meter, consistent with 'No'.

verdicts.question: Is there space available to dig DC, AC and LA earth pits?
verdicts.designer_notes: The setback ground is available on the northwest side of the building (near the inverter room)
verdicts.photo_observation: Unpaved soil setback strip several metres long between the building wall and the boundary/fence wall (pp.9,10), with AC Earth Pit marked on it opposite the inverter room.
verdicts.rationale: Open diggable soil clearly visible next to the inverter room. NW orientation not verifiable from photos.

verdicts.question: What type of Earthing chamber needs to be installed at site? Is it Cement chamber or PVC chamber?
verdicts.photo_observation: Earth pit area is bare soil (pp.9,10); no chamber exists yet and nothing in the photos dictates chamber type.
verdicts.rationale: Chamber type is a design choice, not visually verifiable.

verdicts.question: Are there any challenges with respect to Installation and Maintenance activities?
verdicts.photo_observation: Equipment room is indoor and accessible (p.7), but site is an active construction site: debris and fence panels in the side passage, scaffolding (pp.6,9,10), loose live-looking wiring at meter box (p.10), and no ventilation in the battery room (designer's own E19). No rooftop/PV array photos are provided at all for a 20 kWp system.
verdicts.rationale: Several visible site conditions could pose installation challenges, and the PV array area is undocumented; 'No' cannot be confirmed from the photos.

verdicts.question: Are there any safety risks associated with accessing the roof for installation?
verdicts.photo_observation: No rooftop or roof-access (staircase/ladder) photos in pages 4-12; all roof-detail answers are N/A. Only scaffolding along the side wall is visible.
verdicts.rationale: Roof access is not documented, so 'No safety risks' cannot be verified.

verdicts.question: Is ventilation available in the battery location?
verdicts.designer_notes: Currently there is no ventillation given. But the provision for ventilation will be provided by the customer.
verdicts.photo_observation: Inverter/battery room (pp.7,9) shows plain plastered walls, a sloping (under-stair) ceiling section and a single door; no window, louvre or exhaust opening visible.
verdicts.rationale: No ventilation openings visible, consistent with 'No'; customer-scope ventilation item also listed on p.11.

verdicts.question: Is Battery wall mounted or stand mounted?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.7 markup draws 'BATTERY-3 Nos.' as a box on the wall at mid-height beside the inverter, not on the floor; no stand shown.
verdicts.rationale: Schematic markup position suggests wall placement, which sits awkwardly with 'Stand mounted'; markup may be indicative only - confirm intended battery mounting and floor space for a stand.

verdicts.question: Should the Inverters/ACDB/DCDB be installed on a metal grill or wall mount?
verdicts.photo_observation: p.7 shows INVERTER and Fuse box marked directly on a solid plastered masonry wall in the indoor room; no grill present.
verdicts.rationale: Solid indoor wall is suitable and the markup shows wall mounting.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimensions for solar meter cubicle placement (L x W of wall).
verdicts.photo_observation: p.8 shows wall space beside the main meter where the Input/Output MCB box is marked; no scale reference or measurement visible.
verdicts.rationale: Dimensions cannot be measured from photos.

verdicts.question: Provide the dimension for earth pits location (L x W of available space).
verdicts.photo_observation: Side setback soil strip (pp.9,10) appears roughly 1-1.5 m wide between the building and the boundary wall and extends well beyond 5 m along the building.
verdicts.rationale: Visible strip is consistent with ~5 m x 1 m available; exact measurement not possible from photos.

verdicts.question: Is LAN cable under customer scope?
verdicts.photo_observation: Not photo-verifiable. Observations page (p.11) Customer Scope item 2 lists providing Wi-Fi/LAN connection (note: it refers to an 'Enphase Accessories box' although this is a 20 kWp hybrid system).
verdicts.rationale: Report's customer-scope section corroborates 'Yes'; wording referencing Enphase looks like template carry-over and should be corrected.

verdicts.question: Is the cable routing in the site photos continuous and consistent across the documented run - from rooftop panels to DCDB to inverter to ACDB to solar meter to main panel - with no orphan ends, no unexplained mid-run size changes, and visible conduit / cable-tie / clipping where the run is exposed?
verdicts.designer_notes: No designer answer for this target.
verdicts.photo_observation: Documented legs: inverter room (p.7, purple input/output cable from inverter along floor/under-stair space) -> wall penetration (p.8 top, drilled hole) -> along outer wall to Input/Output MCB box beside main meter (p.8 bottom); AC earthing cable through wall behind door (p.9) to AC Earth Pit (p.9). Cable size stated once (4C x 10 sq.mm Cu flexible, 2 sets). MISSING: no PV array / rooftop photos, no DC cable route from modules to inverter, no DC earth pit, LA, or LA pit markings despite legend entries; no conduit/clipping specification for the exposed outdoor segment to the meter box; solar meter location not marked.
verdicts.rationale: AC side from inverter to meter box and AC earthing are traceable and continuous, but the PV-to-inverter DC run, DC/LA earthing and solar meter are undocumented, so end-to-end continuity cannot be confirmed.
